2023_030_m051623bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held May 16, 2023 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:02 p.m. before an audience of approximately 170 people. The Board recognized district retirees, honored a Student Spotlight artist, adopted resolutions for National Teacher Appreciation Week and Mental Health Awareness Month, and approved three administrative appointments effective July 1, 2023. After roughly an hour of public comment dominated by speakers opposing removal of the honors program, the Board adopted the Illustrative Mathematics materials for middle school grades 6-8 on a 6-1 vote, with Mrs. Anne dissenting.
2023_030_m051623bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held May 16, 2023 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called it to order at 7:02 p.m.; adjournment was at 10:40 p.m. Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson were present with Superintendent Machesky and administrators including Harris, West, DiPilato, and Haezebrouck. Approximately 170 members of the audience attended. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

**Recognitions**
- Retirees: Mr. Harris read each 2022-2023 retiree's name and starting year, among them Karen Barnowski (TSD Preschool, 2003), Monty Clary (Troy High counselor, 1985), Melanie Morey (Principal, Barnard, 2014), Jeremey Whan (Principal, Bemis, 2010), Charles Steltenkamp (Troy High, 1984), and Tony Lucchi (Athens, TEA President, 1996). Each received a gift and certificate.
- Student Spotlight: Katie Redmond, senior at Athens High School, for work through the TSD Creative Guild; Thomas Butcher spoke about it.
- ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting honored the district's Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, crediting Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Kandice Moynihan, Finance Director.

**Resolutions and Appointments**

| Item | Action | Vote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 23-033 | National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 8-12, 2023 | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-034 | Mental Health Awareness Month 2023 | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-034 | Sarah Young, Director, Special Education, two-year probationary contract, July 1, 2023 | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-035 | Karen Bush, Principal, Barnard Elementary, July 1, 2023 | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-036 | Lindsay Keegan, Principal, Schroeder Elementary, July 1, 2023 | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-037 | Consent agenda items A through G | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-038 | Middle school mathematics materials for 2023-2024 | Yes 6, No 1 (Anne) |

The consent agenda covered minutes of the April 4, 2023 Workshop and April 18, 2023 meeting, the Treasurer's Report for March 2023, the Oakland Intermediate School District budget, a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2023/2024 budget, food service contract renewal, and International Academy budget approval for 2023/2024.

**Public Communication**
Given the number of requests, Mr. Schmidt limited each speaker to one and a half minutes, allowing a full hour. Nearly all speakers opposed removal of the honors program; Melissa Sawicke raised exchange student enrollment policy at Troy High and Athens, and Ashleigh Jennings supported the math curriculum changes. Written comments from Kristin Pingree (urging transparency on curriculum changes) and Chris Courtney (supporting the math changes) were read aloud.

**Curriculum**
Christine DiPilato, Natalie Haezebrouck, Kate Rainey, Mark Hayes, Jordan Baines, and Carol Machak presented the proposed Illustrative Mathematics program for grades 6-8, following a detailed May 2 Workshop presentation. Parent learning sessions are planned in buildings during 2023-24. The Board recessed at 9:18 p.m. and resumed at 9:26 p.m.

**Business Approvals**

| Item | Award | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 23-039 | Secure Education Consultants, four-year contract, Director of Security | not stated | designated security dollars, General Fund |
| 23-040 | People Driven Technology, Core Switch replacement and DNA Appliance | $64,386.75 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| 23-041 | Equipment Lease Agreement, copier fleet, up to four years | not to exceed $12,809.00 monthly | General Fund |
| 23-041 | Applied Innovations, Cost per Copy Maintenance, monochrome | not to exceed $.00368 per impression | General Fund |
| 23-042 | Apple Computers, iPads and cases | $855,533 | 2023 Capital Projects Funds |
| 23-043 | Security Designs, elementary security cameras | $577,967 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |

**Announcements**
Dr. Philippart announced the TFEE Golf Outing June 20 at Greystone Golf Club in Washington; Dr. Machesky invited attendance at the Kiwanis Wine Tasting Thursday from 6 to 8:30 at the Troy Historical Society. The next Board Workshop was set for Tuesday, June 6 at the Administration Building and the next regular meeting for Tuesday, June 13 at 7:30 p.m. in the Troy High School Media Center.
2023_030_m051623bdmtg.verbose:
**Identification**
Minutes of a regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held Tuesday, May 16, 2023 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.; the meeting adjourned at 10:40 p.m. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carry the typing reference GH/jh.

**Attendance**
In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Jansen, House, Brinks, Henry, Haezebrouck, Morse, Cross, Duda, Yancy, Roncone, Keyser, Cottone, Canfield, Harris, and West. There were approximately 170 members of the audience.

**Recognition of Troy School District Retirees**
The Board recognized employees who retired or expressed their intention to retire at the end of the 2022-2023 school year. Mr. Harris read each name along with the year the employee's district service began: Karen Barnowski (Teacher, TSD Preschool, since 2003); Marianne Belleville (Teacher, Wass Elementary, since 1996); Sharon Bourdeau (Secretary, International Academy East, since 2011); Monty Clary (Counselor, Troy High, since 1985); Scott Crecelius (Teacher, Larson, since 1990); Bob Dowd (Assistant Principal, Athens, since 1996); Christine Ferguson (Teacher, Athens, since 1994); Maxine Japowicz (Para-Professional, Martell, since 2002); Jill Kelly (Teacher, Larson, since 1996); Tony Lucchi (Teacher/TEA President, Athens, since 1996); Carolyn Maher (Teacher, Wass, since 1990); Diane Miller (Secretary, Boulan Park, since 1995); Joseph Moceri (Teacher, Troy High, since 1994); Melanie Morey (Principal, Barnard, since 2014); Betsy Murphy (Teacher, Hamilton, since 1994); Carolyn Murtagh (Teacher, Larson, since 1999); Barb Pangle (Secretary, Hill, since 2006); Sherri Parks (Teacher, Troy High, since 1988); Mary Pepoy (Secretary, Larson, since 2000); Ellen Podeszwa (Social Worker, Larson, since 2008); Deann Quilliams (Teacher, Larson, since 1988); Virginia Riolo (Teacher, Troy High, since 2004); Mark Sackett (Teacher, Morse, since 1999); Charles Steltenkamp (Teacher, Troy High, since 1984); Nancy Stone (Teacher, Larson, since 1986); Richard Uebbing (Teacher, Baker, since 1987); Michael Webster (Teacher, Troy High, since 1999); Jeremey Whan (Principal, Bemis, since 2010); and Rebecca Yatooma (Teacher, Smith, since 2001). Retirees came forward as their names were read and received congratulations from the Board along with a gift and certificate commemorating their time with the district.

**Student Spotlight**
The monthly Student Spotlight recognized Katie Redmond, a senior at Athens High School, for work produced through the TSD Creative Guild. Thomas Butcher was invited forward to describe the work.

**National Teacher Appreciation Week (Resolution 23-033)**
Teacher Appreciation Week was celebrated Monday, May 8 through Friday, May 12, 2023. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Wilson, the resolution recited that teachers inspire and open children's minds, strengthen the principles of democratic equality, develop leaders and encourage critical thinking, and that Troy teachers set the bar for excellence in education. It resolved that the Troy School District supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 8-12, 2023, and encourages schools and the community to recognize the role of teachers. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Association of School Business Officials' Award (ASBO)**
The Association of School Business Officials International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting Program honored the Troy School District for excellence in the preparation and issuance of a high quality Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022. The Board recognized Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, Kandice Moynihan, Finance Director, and the Finance team for their work.

**Mental Health Awareness Month 2023 (Resolution 23-034)**
The Oakland Community Health Network and its service provider network host annual initiatives promoting community awareness about mental illness, and the district was asked to join other school boards across Oakland County in recognizing May as Mental Health Awareness Month. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Wilson, the resolution recited that mental health is important to individual well-being and to families, communities and schools; that one in five of all Americans, including children, experience mental health issues that could lead to school difficulties, physical problems, and even suicide; and that May 11, 2023 is designated National Children's Mental Health Awareness Day while May 7 through May 13, 2023 is designated Children's Mental Health Acceptance Week. The Board recognized May 2023 as Mental Health Awareness Month. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Personnel**
Mr. Schmidt changed the order of the agenda and moved Personnel up, inviting Mr. Harris to present the administrative positions.
- Director, Special Education (item 23-034): moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Dr. Philippart, that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Sarah Young, beginning duties as Special Education Director effective July 1, 2023. Yes: 7. No: 0.
- Principal, Barnard Elementary School (item 23-035): moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mr. Haupt, that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Karen Bush, effective July 1, 2023. Yes: 7. No: 0.
- Principal, Schroeder Elementary School (item 23-036): moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mr. Haupt, that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Lindsay Keegan, effective July 1, 2023. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Additions and Deletions**
None.

**General Consent Agenda (23-037)**
Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt to approve items A, B, C, D, E, F, and G on the consent agenda: minutes of the April 4, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the April 18, 2023 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for March 2023; approval of the Oakland Intermediate School District budget; a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2023/2024 school year budget; food service contract renewal; and International Academy budget approval for the 2023/2024 school year. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Reports from Student Representatives**
Nish Palepu, student representative for Troy High School, asked for a moment of silence to honor the Troy High student who recently died, then reported on school events and activities. Sara Ali, student representative for Athens High School, reported on events at Athens. Dr. Philippart reported on Troy College and Career High School on behalf of student representative Alexi Papadelis, who was absent. Yara Mashal, student representative for International Academy-East, was also absent.

**Public Communication (Agenda Items)**
Mr. Schmidt explained the guidelines for public comment and, because of the number of requests submitted, limited each speaker to one and a half minutes, allowing a full hour of public comment. Mrs. Melissa Sawicke, a TSD parent, addressed the exchange student enrollment policy at Troy High and Athens. Ms. Ashleigh Jennings, a TSD parent, spoke in support of the new math curriculum changes. The remaining speakers addressed removal of the honors program and supported keeping it as an option for students: Jeff Schaeper, Rocky Raczkowski, Suril Patel, Krish Mathrani (junior at International Academy-East), Tony Cruz, Mark Gunn, Carlo Toppi, Barbara Dawson, Anthony Sarna (sixth grade student at Smith Middle School), Purni Gupta, Yawen Li, Amy Luo, Mei Xu, Angela He, Akul Gunukula (senior at Troy High School), Janice Girling, Andrew Sosnoski, Heugguang Li, Kirit Patel, Tracy Owens, Steven Zheng, Dr. Weilong Hao, George Perakis (senior at Troy High School), Chris Kus, William Wang, Dale Murrish, Yaroslava Ruzankina, Yan Liang, Shivani Angadi (sophomore at Troy High School), and Alex Karpowitscz. Mr. Schmidt read a written communication from TSD parent Kristin Pingree, who stated that Troy Schools are rigorous compared with other districts but asked the district to be more transparent in communicating proposed curriculum changes to parents, and a written communication from TSD parent Chris Courtney supporting the recommended math curriculum changes.

**Curriculum Report: Middle School Math**
Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction; Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching and Learning; Math Curriculum Specialist Kate Rainey; and Math Specialists Mark Hayes, Jordan Baines, and Carol Machak presented a PowerPoint report on the proposed math curriculum Illustrative Mathematics for Grades 6-8. A detailed version had been provided to the Board at the May 2 Workshop, and the full presentation is available for public review on the TSD Math website. It covered the curriculum review process and the program's purpose of allowing students a deeper learning experience, and noted that parent learning sessions will be held in buildings during the 2023-24 school year. Several community concerns were addressed. The Board recessed at 9:18 p.m. and returned at 9:26 p.m. Board and administration discussion covered meeting the needs of all students in one classroom, teachers' ability to teach at all levels, the evaluation process, and professional development to support the new curriculum.

**Middle School Mathematics Materials Adoption (23-038)**
Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Dr. Wilson that the recommended mathematics materials for the middle school level be approved for the 2023-2024 school year. Yes: 6 (Alic, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson). No: 1 (Anne).

**Business: SEC Contract (23-039)**
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Wilson that the Troy Board of Education authorize administration to proceed with finalizing a four-year contract with Secure Education Consultants (SEC) for the purposes of providing a Director of Security and other services outlined in the agreement, to be paid for with designated security dollars in the General Fund. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Business: Network Core Replacement (23-040)**
Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mr. Hauff that the purchase of the Core Switch replacement and DNA Appliance be awarded to People Driven Technology in the amount of $64,386.75, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Business: Copier Replacement (23-041)**
Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Board authorize the Superintendent or designee to negotiate and execute an Equipment Lease Agreement for the purpose of leasing a fleet of copiers for a period no greater than four years at a monthly cost not to exceed $12,809.00; and further that the Superintendent or designee be authorized to negotiate and execute a Cost per Copy Maintenance Agreement with Applied Innovations not to exceed $.00368 per impression for Monochrome Copiers for a period not to exceed four years, with these amounts approved as expenditures of the General Fund. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Business: 2023 iPad Purchase (23-042)**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne that the district purchase iPads and cases from Apple Computers in the amount of $855,533, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Funds. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Business: Elementary Security Cameras (23-043)**
Moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Alic that the purchase of Security Cameras be awarded to Security Designs in the amount of $577,967, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items) and Other**
None was recorded under either heading.

**Board Member Comments**
Dr. Philippart announced the TFEE Golf Outing on June 20 at Greystone Golf Club in Washington. Mr. Haupt expressed support for the Teaching and Learning Department and appreciation for the community. Mr. Hauff mentioned the three presidential scholars who were recently recognized. Dr. Wilson thanked Thomas Butcher for putting Creative Guild on open air to showcase students' talent. Dr. Machesky invited everyone to attend the Kiwanis Wine Tasting event from 6 to 8:30 on Thursday at the Troy Historical Society, noting the funds are used for student-related support. Mr. Schmidt announced that the next Board Workshop would be held Tuesday, June 6 at the Administration Building and the next regular meeting Tuesday, June 13 at 7:30 p.m. in the Troy High School Media Center.

**Adjournment**
The meeting adjourned at 10:40 p.m.
